key_insight: At 12.5% La substitution, enhanced electronic screening in BaTiO₃ weakens ferroelectric polarization and reduces optical anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: Donor substitution offers a design lever for tuning coupled dielectric and optical properties in perovskite oxides.
method: Density functional theory for structural, electronic, and optical properties
Density-functional perturbation theory for phonons and dielectric response
evidence_signal: Calculations show reduced tetragonality and Born effective charges, polar-mode hardening, lower static dielectric response, and an absorption-edge shift consistent with a Burstein–Moss-type mechanism.
watch_item: The findings are computational and limited to 12.5% La substitution; the abstract establishes neither broader doping trends nor AI or solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO$_3$: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy
